title: The bull sent to plow
hook: Shiva's bull garbles a message and is sent to plow; why Pongal thanks the sun and the cattle, and why Hindus honor the cow
carry: thank the ones who feed you: sun and cow

segments.voice: Yesterday, the sun at his son's door, and black sesame. Your line was sankranti mends bonds: sweet sesame, sweet words. Today, Tamil Nadu, and a pot meant to overflow.

Up on Mount Kailash, Shiva gives his bull a simple errand. Nandi, called Basava in this story, is to go down to earth with a message for the people: bathe every day, and eat once a month. Nandi trots down, clears his throat, and announces: Shiva says, bathe once a month, and eat every day! Shiva is not amused. If people are going to eat every day, he says, somebody has to grow all that food. You'll go and plow the fields. And Nandi has been helping the farmers ever since.
screen: `A MESSAGE FROM SHIVA.` → `NANDI GETS IT BACKWARD.` → `SENT TO PLOW.`

segments.voice: That's a folk tale told in Tamil Nadu at Pongal, and it's a funny way of saying something serious. Pongal is Tamil Nadu's harvest festival, on the same days as Sankranti, at the start of the Tamil month of Thai. Pongal means boiling over. A new clay pot of fresh rice, milk and jaggery is set on a fire in the open sun, and when it foams over the side, everyone shouts Pongalo Pongal! The overflow is abundance you can see. And the first pongal goes to Surya, the sun, before anyone eats. The next day is the one the story is about: Mattu Pongal, for the cattle. Cows and bulls are bathed, their horns painted, bells and garlands put on them, and they're fed pongal too. Here's the teaching. Hindus honor the cow. Many call her Go Mata, mother cow, because like a mother she gives: milk, butter, ghee for the lamp, and for centuries a strong back to pull the plow. Krishna grew up herding cows, and Shiva rides a bull. That's a big reason many Hindus don't eat beef, and why you'll see a cow garlanded at a temple. Pongal turns that into days of thanks: first the sun that grew the rice, then the animals that did the work. A Tamil saying for the week: when Thai is born, a way will be born. And today: there's a long line of givers behind every plate you eat from. Pongal says thank them, starting with the ones nobody thanks.
screen: `PONGAL MEANS BOILING OVER.` · `THE FIRST SHARE TO THE SUN.` · `MATTU PONGAL: A DAY FOR THE CATTLE.` · `GO MATA: THE COW WHO GIVES.` · then, large: `THANK THE ONES WHO FEED YOU.`

segments.voice: Before your next meal, or right now in your mind, follow your food backward: the hands that cooked it, the shop, the truck, the farmer, the rain and the sun, and any animal that gave. If you pray, offer the first bite in your heart, the way the first pongal goes to the sun. If you don't, just say thank you, once, to the giver you'd usually forget.
Pongal and Onam, two harvests. Today, Pongal: boiling over. Tamil Nadu's harvest festival, when the new rice spills from a new pot, and the cattle get a day of thanks.
Your line: thank the ones who feed you: sun and cow. The overflow is the blessing. Day one hundred fifty-three, done.

howItsDone: Over four days in the Tamil month of Thai, many Tamil Hindus clear out old things on Bhogi, boil new rice with milk and jaggery until it overflows and offer it to the sun on Thai Pongal, bathe, garland and feed their cattle on Mattu Pongal, and visit family on Kaanum Pongal.
